items.title: Late Fees at the Library
items.text:
A: Excuse me, I'd like to return this novel, but I'm afraid it's four days late.
B: Thanks for telling me. The fine is fifty cents a day, so that's two dollars.
A: Oh, I didn't realize it was due last Friday. Is there any way to avoid the fee?
B: Not this time, but you can renew a book online before the due date. It takes about a minute.
A: I wish someone had told me that. I thought I had to come in person.
B: Many students think so. Here, I'll write the website on this bookmark.
A: That's really helpful. I'll pay the fine today and set a reminder on my phone.
B: Good idea. Would you like to borrow anything else?
A: Yes, the sequel, please. If I need more time, I'll ______.
B: Great. It's due in three weeks.

qs.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
o: A student asks the library to buy a new novel.
A student complains that the fine is too expensive.
A student returns a book and decides never to borrow from this library again.
A student learns how to avoid paying late fees in the future.
qs.why: 책이 늦어 벌금을 내지만, 다음에는 온라인으로 연장할 수 있다는 정보를 얻는 것이 대화의 핵심이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the student?
o: The student often returns books on time.
The student had never renewed a library book online before.
The student works as a volunteer at the library on weekends.
The student dislikes the writer of the novel.
qs.why: 'I wish someone had told me that'과 'I thought I had to come in person'에서 온라인 연장을 몰랐음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Which expression best fills the blank?
o: pay a larger fine at the desk
return it without reading it
renew it online before the due date
ask a friend to borrow it first
qs.why: 앞서 사서가 알려 준 방법을 쓰겠다는 다짐이므로, 기한 전에 온라인으로 연장한다는 말이 자연스러워요.

qs.q: In the conversation, "due" in "it was due last Friday" is closest in meaning to
o: owed as a payment
borrowed for a second time
expected to be returned
damaged by a user
qs.why: 여기서 due는 '(반납) 기한인'이라는 뜻으로, 지난 금요일이 반납 예정일이었다는 말이에요.

qs.q: What does "It" in "It takes about a minute" refer to?
o: walking to the library
writing on a bookmark
renewing a book online
paying the fine
qs.why: 바로 앞 문장의 'renew a book online'을 가리켜요.

items.title: A Short Reply in the Class Chat
items.text:
A: Did you see Jin's message in the class chat? He wrote only "Fine." and nothing else.
B: I saw it. Do you think he's upset about the group project?
A: Maybe. Yesterday he said he'd finished his part, and then we asked him to redo the charts.
B: That could annoy anyone. But in a text it's hard to know. He might just be busy.
A: True. One word can sound cold even when the writer isn't angry at all.
B: Why don't we call him instead of guessing? A voice makes the feeling much clearer.
A: Good plan. I'll also say sorry for the way we asked about the charts.
B: And offer to help with them. Then he'll know we value his work.
A: Right. It's better to clear things up now than let a small problem grow into a ______.
B: Exactly. Let's call him after dinner.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the conversation?
o: Group projects are always easier to finish when every member works alone at home.
Charts should be checked before they are sent to a teacher.
Short written messages can be misunderstood, so speaking directly may help.
Class chats are a good place to argue about schoolwork.
qs.why: 짧은 문자만으로는 감정을 알기 어려우니 전화로 직접 이야기하자는 결론이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the speakers' feelings toward Jin?
o: They are angry that he finished his part of the project too early.
They want him to leave the group.
They care about him and want to treat him fairly.
They think he never reads the chat.
qs.why: 사과하고 도움을 제안하려는 태도에서 Jin을 배려하고 있음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Which expression best fills the blank?
o: funny story
bigger argument
quick reply
new project
qs.why: 작은 문제를 지금 풀지 않으면 커질 수 있다는 흐름이므로 bigger argument가 알맞아요.

qs.q: In the conversation, "cold" in "sound cold" is closest in meaning to
o: low in temperature
unfriendly
tired and sleepy
very quiet
qs.why: 여기서 cold는 기온이 아니라 '냉담한, 쌀쌀맞은'이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What did the group ask Jin to do yesterday?
o: Write a longer message.
Call the others after dinner.
Finish his part sooner.
Make the charts again.
qs.why: 'we asked him to redo the charts'가 근거예요.

items.title: The Green Backpack
items.text:
Clerk: Lost and Found. How can I help you?
Ben: Hi, I left my backpack on the 4:15 train to Eastport. It's dark green with a white tag.
Clerk: Let me check. Do you remember which car you were sitting in?
Ben: The third one, by the window. I got off in a hurry because my phone was about to die.
Clerk: Three bags were turned in this afternoon. One is green, but it has a red zipper.
Ben: That might be mine. The zipper is new. I replaced the old one last month.
Clerk: Can you tell me what's inside?
Ben: A blue notebook, a water bottle, and a calculator with my initials on it.
Clerk: That matches. Please show me your ID and sign here.
Ben: Thank you so much. I was sure I'd never see it again.

qs.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
o: A traveler asks for directions to a train platform.
A traveler gets help to find a bag left on a train.
A clerk explains how to buy a ticket to Eastport.
A traveler complains that a train was late.
qs.why: Ben이 기차에 두고 내린 가방을 분실물 센터에서 찾는 내용이에요.

qs.q: Why did Ben mention the new zipper?
o: To explain why the bag differed from his first description.
To show that he had only just bought the bag at a shop.
To prove that the bag was very expensive and rare.
To ask the clerk to repair the zipper for him.
qs.why: 처음엔 초록색에 흰 태그라고만 했는데 빨간 지퍼가 있어서, 지퍼를 바꿨다고 설명한 거예요.

qs.q: What does the clerk mean by "That matches"?
o: Ben's bag has the same color as the clerk's.
Ben's train ticket is for the right time.
Ben's list fits the things in the bag.
Ben's ID has the same name as his notebook.
qs.why: Ben이 말한 소지품이 가방 안 물건과 일치한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the conversation, "turned in" is closest in meaning to
o: thrown into the trash
turned around quickly
handed over to the staff
bought from a shop
qs.why: turn in은 '(분실물 등을) 제출하다, 맡기다'라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Where was Ben sitting on the train?
o: In the first car, near a door.
In the last car, near the exit.
In the third car, near a window.
In the fourth car, by the aisle.
qs.why: 'The third one, by the window'라고 말했어요.

items.title: Swapping a Shift
items.text:
A: Hi, Mr. Ortiz. Do you have a minute? I need to ask about Saturday's shift at the cafe.
B: Sure. What's the problem?
A: My cousin's graduation is that afternoon, and I promised my family I'd be there.
B: Congratulations to your cousin! Have you asked anyone to cover for you?
A: Yes. Dahlia said she can take my hours if I work her Sunday morning.
B: That sounds fair. But I need to approve any change at least two days ahead.
A: I know, so I came as soon as I could. Is it all right if I write the swap on the schedule?
B: Go ahead. And please text Dahlia so she knows it's official.
A: I will right away. Thanks for being so understanding.
B: No problem. Reliable workers like you make the schedule easy to ______.

qs.q: What is the main point of the conversation?
o: An employee asks for a raise in pay.
A manager decides to close the cafe on Saturday for a family event.
A manager asks an employee to work extra hours.
An employee arranges to trade work hours for a family event.
qs.why: 가족 행사 때문에 동료와 근무를 맞바꾸고 매니저에게 허락을 받는 내용이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Mr. Ortiz?
o: He dislikes it when workers ask for time off to attend family events.
He always refuses to change the schedule.
He plans to work on Sunday morning.
He is willing to be flexible when employees plan ahead.
qs.why: 미리 알리고 대체자도 구한 것을 받아들이는 모습에서 융통성이 있음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Which expression best fills the blank?
o: break
forget
delay
manage
qs.why: 믿을 만한 직원 덕분에 일정을 관리하기 쉽다는 뜻이므로 manage가 자연스러워요.

qs.q: In the conversation, "cover for you" is closest in meaning to
o: keep you out of the rain
hide a secret for you
do your work in your place
pay for your lunch
qs.why: cover for someone은 '대신 근무하다'라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What must the speaker do to get Dahlia's help?
o: Bring a gift to the graduation party.
Work Dahlia's Sunday morning hours.
Buy Dahlia a drink after work on Saturday.
Send the manager a very long email tonight.
qs.why: 'if I work her Sunday morning'이라는 조건이 있어요.

items.title: Too Many Words on the Poster
items.text:
A: Here's the first draft of our poster for the book fair. What do you think?
B: The colors are great, and the drawing of the owl is adorable. But there's a lot of text.
A: I wanted people to know everything: dates, prices, the list of authors, and the raffle rules.
B: I understand, but from across the hallway nobody will read all that.
A: Hmm. So what should we keep?
B: Think about what people need at first glance. The name of the event, the date, and the place.
A: And the rest could go on our website?
B: Exactly. Add a small code that leads to it. Curious students will scan it.
A: Okay, I'll cut the text by half and make the title much bigger.
B: Perfect. A poster should invite people in, not ______ them with details.

qs.q: What is the main point of the conversation?
o: A poster works better when it shows only the most important information.
A poster should include every single detail about an event so nobody is confused.
A drawing of an animal is better than a title.
A website is more useful than any poster.
qs.why: B는 한눈에 보이는 핵심 정보만 남기고 나머지는 웹사이트로 보내라고 조언해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the poster's first draft?
o: It would be hard to read from a distance.
It had no pictures or colors, only a long list of dates.
It was printed on very small paper.
It left out the date of the book fair.
qs.why: 'from across the hallway nobody will read all that'에서 멀리서는 읽기 어렵다는 것을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: welcome
overwhelm
amuse
teach
qs.why: 포스터는 사람들을 끌어들여야지 세부 정보로 압도해서는 안 된다는 흐름이에요.

qs.q: In the conversation, "at first glance" is closest in meaning to
o: after a long discussion
from the first page
in a very quick look
at the beginning of the year
qs.why: at first glance는 '언뜻 보았을 때'라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "it" refer to in "Curious students will scan it"?
o: the owl drawing
the raffle
a small code
the hallway
qs.why: 바로 앞에서 말한 'a small code'를 가리켜요.

items.title: Returning the Wrong Size
items.text:
Customer: Hello, I ordered a medium jacket from your website, but a large one arrived.
Agent: I'm sorry about that. Could you give me your order number?
Customer: It's 48213. I haven't worn it, and the tags are still attached.
Agent: Thank you. I see the mistake in our warehouse. We can send the correct size today.
Customer: Will I need to pay for shipping the large one back?
Agent: No, we'll email a prepaid label. Just put the jacket in any box and drop it at a post office.
Customer: That's a relief. How long will the new jacket take?
Agent: About four days. If it doesn't fit, you can still return it within thirty days.
Customer: Great. I need it for a trip next weekend, so four days is fine.
Agent: Then you'll have it with time to ______. Is there anything else I can help with?

qs.q: What is the main idea of the conversation?
o: A customer asks for a refund because the jacket is old and worn out.
A customer changes the color of a jacket.
A company says it cannot replace the jacket.
A company fixes a customer's order mistake at no extra cost.
qs.why: 잘못 온 사이즈를 회사가 무료로 교환해 주는 내용이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the customer?
o: The customer has already worn the large jacket several times.
The customer plans to buy several more jackets.
The customer wants the right jacket before a trip.
The customer lives next to the warehouse.
qs.why: 'I need it for a trip next weekend'에서 여행 전에 필요함을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Which expression best fills the blank?
o: spare
lose
borrow
argue
qs.why: 여행 전에 여유 시간(time to spare)이 있을 것이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the conversation, "prepaid" in "a prepaid label" most likely means
o: already paid for
difficult to read
sent after the trip
printed on a jacket
qs.why: pre-는 '미리'를 뜻하므로 prepaid는 이미 비용이 지불된 것을 말해요.

qs.q: How long will the new jacket take to arrive?
o: About one day.
About four days.
About thirty days.
About one week.
qs.why: 'About four days'라고 말했어요. 30일은 반품 가능 기간이에요.

items.title: Volunteers for the Community Garden
items.text:
A: Thanks for coming to the community garden meeting, everyone. We have a problem.
B: Is it the water? I noticed the tomatoes looked dry last week.
A: Exactly. Most of us come on Saturdays, so the plants wait all week.
C: Could we make a weekday schedule? I'm free on Tuesday afternoons.
A: That would help. If four people each take one weekday, the garden stays healthy.
B: I can do Wednesdays after school. Maybe the middle school club could join us too.
A: Good thinking. I'll ask their teacher tomorrow.
C: What about the vegetables? Should we share them?
A: Yes. Volunteers can take some home, and the rest will go to the food pantry.
B: That's a nice reward for the work. And it helps neighbors who need it.

qs.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
o: Choosing new vegetables to plant next spring.
Deciding who should lead the middle school club next year.
Making a plan so the garden is cared for every weekday.
Fixing a broken water pipe in the garden.
qs.why: 토요일에만 오는 문제를 해결하려고 평일 당번 일정을 짜는 내용이에요.

qs.q: Why did the speakers decide to ask the middle school club?
o: They need more helpers to share the work.
They want the club to pay for the water.
They plan to move the garden to the school.
They hope the club will buy the vegetables.
qs.why: 요일마다 맡을 사람이 더 필요해서 동아리의 참여를 생각해 낸 거예요.

qs.q: What does speaker B mean by "a nice reward for the work"?
o: The food pantry will pay the volunteers.
The volunteers will win a gardening contest.
The garden will close if nobody works.
Sharing the vegetables is a good way to thank volunteers.
qs.why: 봉사자가 채소를 가져가고 나머지는 기부한다는 말이 보상이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the conversation, "pantry" in "food pantry" is closest in meaning to
o: a room used for school cooking contests
a shop selling garden tools
a school lunch table
a place that gives out food
qs.why: food pantry는 이웃에게 식품을 나눠 주는 곳이에요.

qs.q: When is speaker C free to help?
o: Saturday mornings.
Wednesday afternoons.
Friday evenings.
Tuesday afternoons.
qs.why: C가 'I'm free on Tuesday afternoons'라고 했어요. 수요일은 B예요.

items.title: Finding a Quiet Place to Study
items.text:
A: This cafeteria is so loud. I've read the same paragraph three times.
B: Same here. The band is practicing next door, and everyone is chatting.
A: We have a chemistry quiz tomorrow, and I can't concentrate at all.
B: What if we try the study room on the second floor? Ms. Park said anyone can use it.
A: Do we need to sign up first?
B: Only if you want it for more than an hour. Otherwise, it's first come, first served.
A: Perfect. Let's grab our things before someone else takes it.
B: Wait, can we still talk there? We wanted to quiz each other out loud.
A: I think talking softly is allowed. If not, we can use the hallway bench.
B: Okay. Honestly, a ______ spot matters more than a long time to study.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the conversation?
o: Two students plan a surprise party for a chemistry teacher.
Two students look for a calmer place to prepare for a quiz.
Two students argue about a chemistry grade.
Two students ask a band to play more softly.
qs.why: 시끄러운 식당을 떠나 조용한 자습실을 찾아 퀴즈를 준비하려는 내용이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the study room?
o: It is always full during the day.
Students can often use it without making a reservation.
It is available only to students who are taking chemistry.
It is located next to the music room.
qs.why: 한 시간이 넘을 때만 신청하고 그 외에는 선착순이라고 했어요.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: peaceful
crowded
noisy
distant
qs.why: 소음 때문에 집중이 안 된 상황이므로 '조용한' 장소가 중요하다는 의미예요.

qs.q: In the conversation, "first come, first served" means that
o: the first student must pay a fee
the room opens at a fixed time
people take turns by grade
people who arrive earlier get to use it first
qs.why: 먼저 온 사람이 먼저 이용한다는 뜻의 표현이에요.

qs.q: Who told the students that anyone may use the study room?
o: The band teacher
Another student
Ms. Park
The school nurse
qs.why: B가 'Ms. Park said anyone can use it'이라고 했어요.

items.title: Moving an Appointment
items.text:
Receptionist: Riverside Clinic, how may I help you?
Mina: Hello. I have an appointment tomorrow at ten, but I need to change it.
Receptionist: May I have your full name and birth date?
Mina: Mina Seo, March ninth. My school has a field trip, and I can't miss the bus.
Receptionist: I see. The doctor has an opening Thursday at four or Friday at nine.
Mina: Thursday at four is perfect. Do I have to fast again before the blood test?
Receptionist: Yes. Please don't eat or drink anything except water for eight hours before.
Mina: Okay. Thank you for finding a new time so quickly.
Receptionist: You're welcome. We'll send a text to remind you. And if anything changes, please call at least a day ahead.
Mina: I will. Have a nice afternoon.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the call?
o: To ask the doctor if a field trip is safe for her.
To cancel a blood test for good.
To move a medical appointment to another day.
To pay the bill from the last visit.
qs.why: 현장 학습 때문에 진료 예약을 다른 날로 바꾸려고 전화한 거예요.

qs.q: What can be inferred from the conversation?
o: Mina will have a blood test at the clinic.
Mina will take the school bus to the clinic.
Mina has never visited the clinic.
Mina is the clinic's new doctor.
qs.why: 공복 안내가 있는 것으로 보아 혈액 검사를 받을 예정임을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: What does the receptionist mean by "if anything changes"?
o: if Mina's plans are different again
if the clinic moves to a new building
if the weather becomes cold
if the doctor changes the bus route
qs.why: 일정에 또 변동이 생기면 하루 전에 연락하라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the conversation, "fast" in "fast again" is closest in meaning to
o: run quickly
close the door
wake up early
go without food
qs.why: 여기서 fast는 '금식하다'라는 동사로 쓰였어요.

qs.q: When is Mina's new appointment?
o: Friday at nine.
Tomorrow at ten.
Thursday at nine.
Thursday at four.
qs.why: Mina가 'Thursday at four is perfect'라고 했어요.

items.title: A Suspicious Email
items.text:
A: Mr. Kim, I got an email saying I won a free tablet. It asks me to type my password.
B: Let me see. Hmm, the sender's address looks strange, and the message is full of spelling mistakes.
A: I thought it was strange too. But the prize sounded real.
B: Real companies don't ask for passwords by email. This is a scam.
A: Should I reply and tell them to stop?
B: No. Replying shows that your address is active. Just delete it and mark it as junk.
A: What if I already clicked the link?
B: Then change your password right away and tell your parents. It's better to act quickly.
A: I didn't click it, luckily. I'll show my friends how to spot these.
B: Good. If an offer seems too good to be true, it usually ______.

qs.q: What is the main point of the conversation?
o: Free tablets are given to students at school every single year.
Spelling mistakes are fine in business emails.
Passwords should be shared with teachers.
Offers that ask for private information by email are often scams.
qs.why: 비밀번호를 요구하는 상품 당첨 이메일은 사기라는 것이 핵심이에요.

qs.q: Why does Mr. Kim advise against replying?
o: The company will send a free prize if nobody replies to the email.
The email contains a long message to read.
The reply would cost money.
Replying may show scammers that the address is in use.
qs.why: 답장하면 주소가 활성 상태임을 알려 주게 된다고 했어요.

qs.q: Which expression best fills the blank?
o: is a gift
isn't true
lasts forever
feels cheaper
qs.why: '너무 좋아서 믿기 어려운 제안은 보통 사실이 아니다'라는 관용적 흐름이에요.

qs.q: In the conversation, "spot" in "how to spot these" is closest in meaning to
o: clean
create
recognize
avoid wearing
qs.why: 여기서 spot은 '발견하다, 알아보다'라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What should a person do if he or she already clicked the link?
o: Change the password and tell a parent.
Reply to the sender quickly.
Delete the email and wait.
Buy a new tablet at once.
qs.why: 'change your password right away and tell your parents'가 근거예요.

items.title: Starting an Internship
items.text:
A: Welcome to the design studio, Yuna. Your desk is by the window.
B: Thank you. I'm a little nervous. I don't want to make mistakes on my first day.
A: Everyone makes some. The important thing is to ask questions early rather than guess.
B: Even if the question seems simple?
A: Especially then. A short question now can save hours of fixing later.
B: That makes sense. Is there anything I should read first?
A: Yes. This folder explains how we name our files. It looks boring, but it keeps the team organized.
B: I'll read it at lunch. When is the team meeting?
A: Tomorrow at nine. You don't need to prepare. Just listen and take notes.
B: Got it. I'm already feeling more ______.

qs.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
o: A worker is saying goodbye before leaving for another job.
A manager is complaining about late files.
A new intern is given advice to help her start well.
A student is choosing a new design school.
qs.why: 인턴에게 첫날 도움이 되는 조언을 해 주는 대화예요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the speaker who greets Yuna?
o: This person is also starting today.
This person has never used the folder.
This person works at a different company in the same city.
This person has been working at the studio for some time.
qs.why: 책상, 폴더, 회의를 안내하는 모습에서 이미 스튜디오에서 일해 온 사람임을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: nervous
hungry
surprised
comfortable
qs.why: 조언을 듣고 긴장이 풀렸다는 흐름이므로 comfortable이 알맞아요.

qs.q: In the conversation, "organized" most likely means
o: very expensive
hard to find
finished early
arranged in a clear way
qs.why: 파일 이름 규칙은 팀의 자료를 정돈된 상태로 유지해 줘요.

qs.q: What does the speaker say Yuna should do at tomorrow's meeting?
o: Listen and take notes.
Present her first design.
Read the folder aloud.
Introduce each team member.
qs.why: 'Just listen and take notes'가 근거예요.

items.title: The Permission Slip
items.text:
Teacher: Dan, I haven't received your permission slip for the museum trip. It's due tomorrow.
Dan: I'm sorry, Ms. Cho. I gave it to my mom last week, but she forgot to sign it.
Teacher: Do you think she can sign it tonight?
Dan: She works late, but I'll leave it on the kitchen table with a note.
Teacher: Good. Without a signature, I can't let you board the bus.
Dan: I understand. Is the trip still on if it rains?
Teacher: Yes. We'll spend most of the day inside, so you won't need an umbrella.
Dan: What about lunch? Should I bring one?
Teacher: Yes, and a water bottle. The museum cafe is small, so bringing your own food is easier.
Dan: Thanks. I'll make sure the slip is back on your desk first thing tomorrow.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the conversation?
o: A student wants to cancel his place on the museum trip today.
A student is reminded of what he must do before a school trip.
A teacher changes the date of the museum visit.
A teacher asks parents to pay for lunch.
qs.why: 허가서 제출과 준비물을 안내받는 내용이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Dan's mother?
o: She refuses to let him go on the trip to the museum.
She is busy and forgot to sign the form.
She works at the museum.
She will drive Dan to school.
qs.why: 늦게까지 일하고 서명을 깜빡했다고 했어요.

qs.q: What does "still on" mean in Dan's question "Is the trip still on if it rains?"
o: The trip begins in the afternoon.
The bus will wait for Dan.
The trip will not be cancelled.
The museum is turning on its lights.
qs.why: 비가 와도 여행이 취소되지 않고 진행된다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the conversation, "board" in "board the bus" is closest in meaning to
o: clean
paint
leave
get on
qs.why: board는 '(차·배에) 타다'라는 동사예요.

qs.q: Why does the teacher suggest bringing lunch?
o: The trip will last two weeks.
Students must pay for food.
The museum cafe is small.
The cafe is closed for repairs.
qs.why: 박물관 카페가 작아서 도시락이 더 편하다고 했어요.

items.title: Noise from the Apartment Above
items.text:
A: Hi, Mr. Reyes. I'm Laura from apartment 4B. Do you have a moment?
B: Of course. Is something wrong?
A: Not exactly. I wanted to mention that I can hear music late at night, usually around eleven.
B: Oh no, I had no idea it traveled that far. I'm so sorry.
A: It's not a big problem, but I have an early shift at the hospital, and sleep matters.
B: I completely understand. I often wear headphones, but last week mine broke.
A: Then maybe you could lower the volume after ten until you buy new ones?
B: Definitely. I'll order a pair tonight. Please knock if it ever bothers you again.
A: Thanks. I appreciate your being so kind about it.
B: Not at all. It's easier to live together when we talk openly.

qs.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
o: Two neighbors plan a party in the building.
A neighbor wants to move to a quieter apartment soon.
Two coworkers discuss a hospital shift.
A neighbor politely asks someone to keep the noise down.
qs.why: 밤늦은 음악 소리 문제를 이웃이 정중하게 이야기하는 내용이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Mr. Reyes?
o: He plays loud music on purpose to annoy Laura.
He did not know his music disturbed his neighbor.
He works at the hospital with Laura.
He lives on the same floor as Laura.
qs.why: 'I had no idea it traveled that far'에서 몰랐음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: What does Laura mean by "sleep matters"?
o: She enjoys dreaming at night.
Getting enough rest is important for her job.
She wants to buy a better bed.
She prefers listening to music.
qs.why: 이른 근무 때문에 충분한 잠이 중요하다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the conversation, "bothers" in "if it ever bothers you" is closest in meaning to
o: helps
greets
follows
disturbs
qs.why: bother는 '귀찮게 하다, 방해하다'라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why did Mr. Reyes stop using headphones recently?
o: They broke last week.
They were too expensive.
They were lost at the hospital.
They gave him a headache.
qs.why: 'last week mine broke'가 근거예요.

items.title: Practicing a Presentation
items.text:
A: Do you have time to listen to my presentation on solar energy? It's on Monday.
B: Sure. Go ahead, and I'll take notes.
A: Okay. First, I explain how panels turn sunlight into electricity. Then I compare the costs.
B: Wait, can I stop you? You are reading directly from your cards.
A: I get nervous, so I memorize every word.
B: Try looking at the class instead. If you forget a line, just say the main idea in your own words.
A: That sounds scary. What if I lose my place?
B: Then take a breath and smile. Honestly, the audience rarely notices a short pause.
A: Okay. Let me try the introduction again without the cards.
B: Much better! You sounded confident and natural that time.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the conversation?
o: A student learns why solar panels are so expensive to build.
A student decides to skip the presentation.
A student gets advice to present in a more natural way.
A student teaches a friend to memorize speeches.
qs.why: 카드를 읽지 말고 청중을 보며 자연스럽게 말하라는 조언이 중심이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the speaker giving the presentation?
o: The speaker is the teacher who grades the class.
The speaker has given many talks before.
The speaker is anxious about speaking in front of people.
The speaker dislikes the topic of solar energy very much.
qs.why: 'I get nervous, so I memorize every word'에서 긴장함을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: What does B mean by "the audience rarely notices a short pause"?
o: A brief silence is not a big problem.
The audience falls asleep quickly.
The audience cannot hear the speaker.
A speaker should never stop talking.
qs.why: 짧은 멈춤은 청중이 거의 알아차리지 못하므로 괜찮다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the conversation, "confident" is closest in meaning to
o: easily confused
very tired
sure of oneself
slightly angry
qs.why: confident는 '자신감 있는'이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: When will the presentation take place?
o: On Friday.
Tomorrow morning.
Next month.
On Monday.
qs.why: A가 'It's on Monday'라고 말했어요.

items.title: The Clothes Swap
items.text: Every spring, our school holds a clothes swap in the gym. Students bring jackets, shirts, and shoes they no longer wear, and they leave with something new to them. At first, some people thought the idea was strange. They worried that used clothes were not good enough. However, the event has grown so popular that many students now arrive an hour early. The organizers say the swap does more than save money. The fashion industry uses huge amounts of water and energy, and many clothes are thrown away after only a few wearings. By giving garments a second life, students can reduce waste without giving up style. As one organizer put it, "The cheapest and greenest clothes are the ones that already ______." Even students who bring nothing are welcome to take a few items, because the goal is sharing, not scoring.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Students should stop wearing fashionable clothes and buy plain ones.
The school gym needs more space for clothes.
New clothes are always better than used ones.
Swapping clothes can be a fun way to save money and cut waste.
qs.why: 옷 교환 행사가 비용도 아끼고 쓰레기도 줄인다는 것이 중심 내용이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the clothes swap?
o: It started small but became more popular over time.
It is held only for students who have no clothes of their own.
It is opposed by most students today.
It charges a high fee at the gym door.
qs.why: 처음엔 이상하게 여겼지만 이제는 한 시간 일찍 오는 학생이 많다고 했어요.

qs.q: Which expression best fills the blank?
o: break
exist
shrink
change colors
qs.why: 가장 저렴하고 친환경적인 옷은 '이미 존재하는' 옷이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, "garments" is closest in meaning to
o: kinds of cloth machines
pieces of clothing
small garden tools
school uniforms only
qs.why: giving garments a second life는 옷에게 두 번째 삶을 준다는 의미로, garment는 의류예요.

qs.q: According to the passage, who may take items at the swap?
o: Only students who arrive at noon
Only the organizers of the event
Even students who bring nothing
Only people from other schools
qs.why: 마지막 문장에서 아무것도 가져오지 않은 학생도 환영한다고 했어요.

items.title: Why Geese Fly in a V
items.text: If you have ever watched wild geese in autumn, you have probably noticed their V-shaped formation. For a long time people thought it was just a pattern, but scientists have found a practical reason. The bird at the front pushes through the air and creates swirls that lift the birds behind it. By flying in the right place, each goose receives a little extra support and saves energy. This matters because their journeys can last thousands of kilometers. The leader works hardest, so the geese regularly change positions. A tired bird slides back, and a rested one moves forward. Researchers believe this teamwork helps the whole flock arrive in better condition than a single bird could manage alone. In other words, the V is not decoration; it is a smart way to ______.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How geese choose a place to build nests
Why geese gain an advantage by flying in a V shape
Why geese must travel thousands of kilometers each year
How scientists count birds in the sky
qs.why: 기러기가 V자 대형으로 날며 에너지를 절약하는 이유를 설명해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the goose at the front?
o: It is always the oldest and strongest bird in the flock.
It rests more than the birds behind it.
Its position is tiring, so others take its place later.
It never needs help during the journey.
qs.why: 리더가 가장 힘들어서 정기적으로 자리를 바꾼다고 했어요.

qs.q: Which expression best fills the blank?
o: avoid the wind
hide from enemies
share the effort
make more noise
qs.why: 앞 내용 전체를 요약하면 V자 대형은 노력(에너지)을 나눠 쓰는 방법이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, "formation" is closest in meaning to
o: an arranged pattern
a sudden accident
a loud sound
a long rest
qs.why: formation은 일정한 모양으로 배열된 대형을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What does "it" refer to in "For a long time people thought it was just a pattern"?
o: the autumn weather
the air near the ground
the front goose
the V-shaped formation
qs.why: 문장 앞부분에서 말한 V자 대형을 가리켜요.

items.title: Can You Trust Online Reviews?
items.text: Before buying a product, most of us check online reviews. A high score makes us feel safe, and a low one makes us look elsewhere. But reviews are not always honest. Some companies pay people to write praise, and some competitors post false complaints. Even real reviews can be misleading, because people who are extremely happy or extremely angry are more likely to write than people with ordinary experiences. So a score of 4.8 may hide the fact that only a few buyers responded. Experts suggest a few habits. Look at how many reviews there are, read some of the middle ratings, and notice whether the comments give specific details. A review that says "Great!" tells you little, while one explaining how a bag survived a rainy month is far more ______.

qs.q: What is the main point of the passage?
o: Companies should stop selling products online and open more shops.
Low scores always mean that a product is unsafe or dangerous.
Most reviewers write long and detailed comments.
Online reviews should be read carefully instead of trusted blindly.
qs.why: 리뷰가 항상 정직하진 않으니 신중히 읽어야 한다는 것이 핵심이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about a 4.8 score from only a few buyers?
o: It may not show how most customers really feel.
It proves the product is perfect.
It means the company paid every buyer to give a high score.
It shows that the product is cheap.
qs.why: 소수의 응답만으로는 전체 구매자의 의견을 대표하지 못할 수 있어요.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: boring
careless
private
useful
qs.why: 구체적인 설명이 있는 리뷰가 '더 유용하다'는 대비 흐름이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, "misleading" is closest in meaning to
o: giving a false idea
very long and slow
difficult to find
easy to copy
qs.why: misleading은 '오해하게 만드는'이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: According to the passage, why might extreme reviews be more common?
o: Companies refuse to publish ordinary opinions here.
Very happy or very angry people are more likely to write.
Most buyers never receive their orders on time.
Reviewers get a small reward for short comments.
qs.why: 극단적인 경험을 한 사람이 리뷰를 더 잘 쓴다고 했어요.

items.title: Sorting Cans at the Food Bank
items.text: Jae-won signed up to volunteer at the food bank because his school required thirty hours of community service. He expected a boring afternoon of lifting boxes. On the first day, a supervisor named Mrs. Alvarez handed him a pair of gloves and pointed to a mountain of canned goods. "Check the dates," she said. "Anything expired goes in the red bin." Jae-won worked quietly for two hours. Then a family came to collect their groceries, and a boy about his little brother's age thanked him for the peaches. Jae-won felt his face grow warm. He had never thought about who would eat the food he was sorting. When the shift ended, he asked Mrs. Alvarez if he could come back on Sunday, even though the hours would not count for school. He did not need the credit anymore; he had found ______.

qs.q: What is the story mainly about?
o: A student quits volunteering because the work is too tiring.
A student discovers meaning in work he first thought was dull.
A supervisor teaches a boy how to sort peaches.
A family donates canned goods to a school.
qs.why: 처음엔 지루하다고 생각했지만 봉사의 의미를 발견하는 이야기예요.

qs.q: Why did Jae-won's face grow warm?
o: He felt moved by the boy's thanks.
He was embarrassed about a mistake.
He was tired from lifting boxes.
He was angry at the supervisor.
qs.why: 아이가 고맙다고 하자 마음이 뭉클해진 거예요.

qs.q: Which expression best fills the blank?
o: a reason of his own
a faster way to sort
an easy way to earn credit
a gift for his brother
qs.why: 학교 시간 인정이 필요 없어졌다는 것은 스스로의 이유를 찾았다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, "expired" most likely describes food that
o: is past its safe date
is too heavy for one person to lift
has been paid for
came from a farm
qs.why: 날짜를 확인해 기한이 지난 것을 빨간 통에 넣으라는 지시예요.

qs.q: Why did Jae-won first join the food bank?
o: His little brother worked there.
He wanted to eat peaches.
His school required community service hours.
Mrs. Alvarez asked him to come.
qs.why: 첫 문장에서 학교가 봉사 30시간을 요구했다고 해요.

items.title: Notice: Changes to the Library Schedule
items.text:
Dear students and families,
Starting October 1, the school library will change its opening hours. The library will open at 7:45 a.m. instead of 8:30 a.m. and will close at 4:00 p.m. on weekdays. On Wednesdays, however, it will stay open until 6:00 p.m. for students who need a quiet place to finish homework after clubs. We made these changes after a survey showed that many students wanted morning access to computers before class. Please note that younger students must be accompanied by an older student or a teacher after 4:00 p.m. Late returns can be placed in the box outside the main door, but books left there after closing will be recorded the following morning. We hope the new schedule will serve you better. If you have questions, please ______ the library desk or send an email.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of this notice?
o: To ask students and families for new book donations
To explain how students can join a school club
To announce new opening hours for the library
To warn students about overdue book fines
qs.why: 도서관 운영 시간 변경을 알리는 공지예요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the Wednesday hours?
o: The library is closed on Wednesdays.
Only teachers and parents may use the library on that day.
The library is open later to help students after club activities.
Students may borrow more books than usual on Wednesday.
qs.why: 동아리 후 숙제를 할 수 있도록 수요일에는 늦게까지 연다고 했어요.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: avoid
paint
visit
throw
qs.why: 질문이 있으면 도서관 데스크를 방문하거나 이메일을 보내라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the notice, "accompanied" is closest in meaning to
o: warned by
joined by
followed by a bell
taught by
qs.why: accompanied by는 '~와 동행한'이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: According to the notice, why were the changes made?
o: The library needed to save electricity.
Many students wanted to use computers before class.
Teachers asked for a longer lunch break.
The survey asked for fewer books.
qs.why: 설문 결과 아침에 컴퓨터를 쓰고 싶은 학생이 많았다고 해요.

items.title: Panels on the Gym Roof
items.text: Last year, the town of Brookfield placed solar panels on the roof of its public gym. Many residents questioned the plan because the panels were expensive and the town had other needs. Engineers explained that the gym uses a lot of electricity for lights and heaters, and that its large flat roof catches a great deal of sunshine. After twelve months, the gym's power bill had dropped by nearly forty percent. The savings were used to buy new basketballs and repair the swimming pool. The mayor said the project proved that a cost can become an investment if it is planned carefully. Some residents still think the panels look ugly, but few deny the benefits. Other towns have begun asking Brookfield for advice, hoping to follow its ______.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A town's solar panels reduced costs and brought other benefits.
A town decided to close its public gym to save money.
Engineers argued about the shape of a roof.
A swimming pool was built with a new roof.
qs.why: 체육관 지붕의 태양광 패널이 전기 요금을 줄이고 이점을 가져왔다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the residents' opinions?
o: They all supported the plan from the very beginning of it.
They became more positive, though not everyone liked the look.
They wanted the gym to be built elsewhere.
They never paid attention to the power bill.
qs.why: 처음에는 의문을 가졌지만 이점은 부정하기 어렵고 일부는 외관을 싫어한다고 해요.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: mistake
accident
order
example
qs.why: 다른 도시가 조언을 구하고 Brookfield의 본보기를 따르려 한다는 흐름이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, "investment" is closest in meaning to
o: a loud complaint from a crowd
money spent that brings later benefits
a gift that must be returned
a plan that was cancelled
qs.why: 투자는 비용을 쓰지만 나중에 이익을 얻는 것을 뜻해요.

qs.q: What was done with the money saved?
o: It paid for a new mayor's office.
It was returned to the engineers.
It bought basketballs and fixed the pool.
It built a second gym.
qs.why: 절약한 돈으로 농구공을 사고 수영장을 수리했다고 해요.

items.title: Noise and the Student Brain
items.text: Many students claim they study best with loud music in their ears. Researchers who tested this idea found that the truth is more complicated. When people read difficult material, music with lyrics competes with the words on the page, because the brain has to handle two kinds of language at once. As a result, understanding goes down. Calm music without words has a smaller effect, and for simple, repeated tasks such as copying notes, some people even work faster with background sound. The key difference is the type of task. Reading a science chapter demands deep thinking, while tidying a desk does not. Therefore, experts recommend that students choose their audio to match the job. Silence is not always necessary, but when the material is hard, it is usually safer to ______.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Loud music helps students understand every school subject better.
The best background sound depends on the type of study task.
Students should always study in complete silence at a library.
Copying notes is harder than reading science.
qs.why: 과제의 종류에 따라 배경 소리가 도움이 되기도 해롭기도 한다는 것이 요지예요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about music with lyrics?
o: It helps students memorize long word lists more easily.
It makes even simple tasks impossible to finish.
It is banned in most school and public libraries.
It may interfere with reading because both use language.
qs.why: 가사가 있는 음악은 글과 함께 언어 처리를 경쟁하게 해 이해를 떨어뜨려요.

qs.q: Which expression best fills the blank?
o: keep the sound low or turn it off
add more words to the music
study in a louder place
listen to several songs at once
qs.why: 어려운 자료일 때는 소리를 줄이거나 끄는 것이 안전하다는 결론이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, "demands" is closest in meaning to
o: refuses politely
forgives
requires
sells
qs.why: 여기서 demand는 '요구하다, 필요로 하다'라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: According to the passage, which task may go faster with background sound?
o: Reading a science chapter
Copying notes
Writing a long essay
Solving a hard puzzle
qs.why: 단순 반복 작업인 노트 베끼기는 소리가 있으면 더 빨리 하는 사람도 있다고 해요.

items.title: The Statue That Wasn't Finished
items.text: In the center of the town square stands a statue with a rough, unfinished face. Visitors often ask why the sculptor stopped. According to local stories, the artist, an older man named Carlo, was carving a famous teacher when winter arrived. His hands were too stiff to continue, and he promised to return in the spring. Spring came, but Carlo did not feel well enough to climb the scaffold. Before he passed away, he asked the town not to hire anyone else. "Let the people remember that every good thing needs time," he said. Today, children touch the rough stone and make wishes, and the town holds a small festival each April. Many agree that the unfinished face tells a stronger story than a perfect one could. Its message is that progress matters more than ______.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: How an old man learned to carve stone during the winter
The reason a town keeps an unfinished statue and what it means
A famous teacher who later became a sculptor of statues
A spring festival that was cancelled forever by the town
qs.why: 미완성 조각상이 남은 이유와 그것이 담은 의미를 이야기해요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the town's feelings toward the statue?
o: They treasure it because of its story.
They plan to replace it with a new one.
They are embarrassed by the rough face.
They want a stranger to finish it.
qs.why: 매년 축제를 열고 아이들이 소원을 비는 것에서 소중히 여김을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: patience
perfection
friendship
weather
qs.why: 미완성의 이야기가 더 강하다는 흐름이므로 완벽함보다 과정이 중요하다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, "scaffold" most likely refers to
o: a rare type of stone from the hills
a heavy bag of carving tools
a town festival
a frame workers stand on
qs.why: 조각가가 올라가야 했던 작업용 발판이에요.

qs.q: When does the town hold its festival?
o: Every winter
Each April
On Carlo's birthday
In the middle of summer
qs.why: 'a small festival each April'이 근거예요.

items.title: The Day the Printer Broke
items.text: Sofia had spent three nights working on her science report, and it was due at nine o'clock. At eight forty, she stood in front of the school printer, which blinked a red light and refused to cooperate. Her heart sank. A classmate named Leo noticed her panic and offered his laptop to email the file to the teacher. Sofia hesitated. She had always insisted on handing in paper copies because she believed they looked more serious. But the clock was ticking, so she agreed. Two minutes later, the email was sent. At nine, the teacher wrote back saying the report had arrived and looked excellent. Sofia laughed with relief. Later she told Leo, "I learned something today: being flexible can be more important than being ______."

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Sofia learned that adapting to a problem can matter more than sticking to a plan.
Sofia lost her science report somewhere on the way to school that morning.
Leo wanted to borrow Sofia's printer to finish his own homework.
The teacher refused to accept an email and demanded a paper copy.
qs.why: 프린터가 고장 나자 방식을 바꿔 제출한 경험에서 융통성의 중요성을 깨달아요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Sofia before the printer broke?
o: She usually preferred paper copies for important work.
She had not started working on the report yet.
She did not know Leo.
She often handed in assignments late.
qs.why: 'always insisted on handing in paper copies'에서 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: flexible
helpful
thankful
strict
qs.why: 유연함이 더 중요하다는 대조이므로 '엄격한, 고집스러운'이 와야 해요.

qs.q: In the passage, "hesitated" is closest in meaning to
o: jumped up with great joy
spoke very loudly to the class
left the room
paused because she was unsure
qs.why: hesitate는 확신이 없어 망설이는 것을 뜻해요.

qs.q: In the passage, "which" in "which blinked a red light" refers to
o: the science report
the red light
the clock
the school printer
qs.why: 관계대명사 which는 앞의 'the school printer'를 가리켜요.

items.title: What Tree Rings Tell Us
items.text: When a tree is cut down, its trunk shows a pattern of circles called rings. Each ring usually represents one year of growth. In a year with plenty of rain, the tree grows quickly and forms a wide ring. In a dry year, growth slows, and the ring is thin. By counting and measuring the rings, scientists can learn not only how old a tree is but also what the climate was like long ago. Sometimes a ring has a dark scar, which may show that a fire passed through the forest. Because some trees live for hundreds of years, their trunks work like diaries written in wood. Researchers compare rings from many trees to build a record that stretches far into the past. These records help us understand how weather has ______ over time.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why trees need more rain every year
How to protect forests from fires
Which kinds of trees live the longest in the world
How tree rings reveal a tree's age and past conditions
qs.why: 나이테로 나무의 나이와 과거 기후를 알 수 있다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred if a ring is very thin?
o: The tree was cut down earlier than most trees.
The tree grew during a very rainy season.
The tree probably had little water that year.
The tree was older than its neighbors.
qs.why: 건조한 해에는 성장이 느려 얇은 나이테가 생긴다고 했어요.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: changed
stopped
hidden
improved
qs.why: 과거의 기록으로 날씨가 시간에 따라 어떻게 변해 왔는지 이해한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, "stretches" in "stretches far into the past" is closest in meaning to
o: pulls tight
jumps over
breaks apart
reaches back
qs.why: 여기서 stretch는 어떤 시점까지 '이어지다, 거슬러 올라가다'라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what might a dark scar in a ring show?
o: That the tree grew much too fast
That the tree was moved
That a fire passed through the forest
That the winter was unusually short
qs.why: 어두운 흉터는 숲에 불이 지나갔음을 보여 줄 수 있다고 했어요.

items.title: Rest Days Make Athletes Stronger
items.text: Many young athletes believe that training every day is the fastest way to improve. Coaches and doctors disagree. When you exercise hard, tiny tears appear in your muscles, and your energy supplies run low. It is during rest, not during practice, that the body repairs these tears and grows stronger. Athletes who skip rest days often feel tired, play worse, and are more likely to be injured. Sleep also plays a key role, since much of the body's repair work happens at night. This does not mean that rest days must be spent on the sofa. Light activities such as walking or stretching can help blood flow without causing stress. A good training plan, therefore, includes recovery as an essential part rather than a sign of ______.

qs.q: What is the main point of the passage?
o: Rest is an important part of getting stronger in sports.
Athletes should train for as many hours as possible each day.
Sleep is more enjoyable than any exercise.
Doctors should coach every sports team.
qs.why: 휴식 중에 몸이 회복되어 강해지므로 휴식도 훈련의 일부라는 것이 핵심이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about an athlete who never rests?
o: The athlete will win every competition.
The athlete is likely to get hurt or play poorly.
The athlete gets more sleep than others.
The athlete does not need to stretch.
qs.why: 휴식을 건너뛰면 피로, 부진, 부상 위험이 커진다고 했어요.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: laziness
strength
progress
safety
qs.why: 회복은 필수 요소이지 게으름의 표시가 아니라는 흐름이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, "tears" refers to
o: drops of water from the eyes
small breaks in the muscle
loud complaints from the coach
parts of a uniform
qs.why: 여기서 tears는 근육의 미세한 손상(찢어짐)을 뜻해요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what light activity is suggested on a rest day?
o: Running a long race
Walking or stretching
Lifting heavy weights
Playing a full match
qs.why: 휴식일에 걷기나 스트레칭 같은 가벼운 활동을 권해요.

items.title: Leftovers on the Lunch Tray
items.text: At Hillside High School, the cafeteria staff noticed that the trash cans were full of untouched fruit, half-eaten sandwiches, and unopened milk cartons. A student council team decided to measure the problem. For one week, they weighed everything thrown away after lunch. The total was more than two hundred kilograms. Surprised, they surveyed classmates and learned that many students took more than they could eat because the lunch line moved fast and they feared missing out. The team suggested three changes: smaller starting portions with free second helpings, a "share table" for sealed items, and signs showing how much food was discarded each day. Within a month, the weekly waste dropped by almost half. The principal praised the plan, noting that solving a problem begins with ______ it.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: The cafeteria decided to stop serving fruit and sandwiches.
Students found a way to reduce food waste at their school.
A principal punished students for wasting food at lunch.
A new lunch line was built for faster service.
qs.why: 학생회가 급식 잔반 문제를 측정하고 해결책으로 줄인 이야기예요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the students who took too much food?
o: They disliked every item on the menu that week.
They did so because they worried about not getting enough.
They wanted to save food for dinner.
They were told to take two portions.
qs.why: 줄이 빨리 움직여 놓칠까 봐 더 많이 담았다고 했어요.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: ignoring
decorating
forgetting
measuring
qs.why: 문제를 해결하는 첫걸음은 이를 측정(파악)하는 것이라는 맥락이에요. 학생들이 먼저 무게를 쟀어요.

qs.q: In the passage, "discarded" is closest in meaning to
o: carefully stored
freshly cooked
thrown away
politely shared
qs.why: discard는 '버리다'라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What was the purpose of the share table?
o: To let students leave sealed items for others
To weigh the trash after each lunch
To sell leftover sandwiches to teachers
To store the principal's notes
qs.why: 포장된 음식을 다른 학생이 가져갈 수 있게 두는 테이블이에요.

items.title: Music in the Subway
items.text: Every morning at Central Station, a violinist sets up near the stairs and begins to play. Most commuters hurry past with their heads down. Some glance over, and a few drop coins into the open case. A city survey once asked travelers about street performers. Many said they enjoyed the music but rarely stopped, because they were afraid of being late. Yet those who paused for just a minute reported feeling calmer for the rest of the day. City officials now give permits to selected performers, hoping to make stations feel friendlier. Some critics worry that music might block the walkways, but the permit rules require artists to stay in designated spots. For the violinist, the reward is not only money. As she says, "A single smile from a stranger is enough to make my ______ worthwhile."

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Violinists earn more money than most other workers in a large city.
Commuters should never stop to listen to or talk with street performers.
Street music in stations can improve people's day, and the city supports it with rules.
Stations are far too crowded to allow any kind of music to be played.
qs.why: 역에서의 거리 음악이 사람들의 기분을 좋게 하고 도시가 허가제로 지원한다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about most commuters?
o: They dislike all kinds of music being played in public places.
They know the violinist personally because they went to school with her.
They enjoy the music but are in too much of a hurry to stop.
They usually give large amounts of money to the performer.
qs.why: 음악을 즐기지만 지각할까 봐 멈추지 않는다고 했어요.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: luggage
coat
ticket
morning
qs.why: 낯선 이의 미소 하나만으로도 아침(의 연주)이 가치 있다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: In the passage, "permits" in "give permits to selected performers" is closest in meaning to
o: official permissions
musical instruments for beginners
small gifts
free tickets
qs.why: permit은 '허가증'을 뜻해요.

qs.q: According to the passage, where must performers stay?
o: Near the ticket gates
On top of the stairs
Inside the trains
In designated spots
qs.why: 허가 규칙은 지정된 장소에만 있으라고 요구해요.

items.title: Message to the New Interns
items.text:
Subject: Welcome and a few reminders
Dear interns,
Welcome to the marketing team! We are happy to have you for the summer. Before your first week, here are a few reminders about how we work. Our team meets online every Monday at ten, so please join on time with your camera on if you can. If you cannot attend, send a short message beforehand. When you write emails to clients, always ask a teammate to read them first; a second pair of eyes catches errors you might miss. Please do not hesitate to ask questions in the team chat, because nobody expects you to know everything yet. Finally, take your breaks. Tired people produce poor work, and we would rather see you refreshed than exhausted. We are confident that you will learn quickly, and we look forward to your ______.
Best wishes,
Grace Tan

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the message?
o: To announce that the summer program has been cancelled
To welcome new interns and explain how the team works
To ask clients to join a Monday meeting
To complain about errors in a report
qs.why: 신입 인턴을 환영하고 팀의 업무 방식을 안내하는 글이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the team's attitude toward mistakes?
o: They expect interns to know everything on the first day.
They accept that beginners need to ask for help.
They want interns to avoid the team chat.
They will reject any email with an error.
qs.why: 아직 모든 걸 알 필요 없다며 질문을 권하는 데서 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Which word best fills the blank?
o: complaints
ideas
excuses
absences
qs.why: 인턴이 빨리 배울 것이라고 확신하며 그들의 기여(ideas)를 기대한다는 흐름이에요.

qs.q: In the message, "refreshed" is closest in meaning to
o: full of energy again
very busy with work
slightly late
difficult to see
qs.why: refreshed는 휴식을 취해 기운을 되찾은 상태를 말해요.

qs.q: According to the message, what should interns do before sending a client email?
o: Wait until Monday at ten o'clock
Ask a teammate to read it
Print it out for the manager
Call the client first
qs.why: 고객에게 보내기 전에 동료에게 읽어 달라고 하라고 했어요.
